journal: TRANSPORTATION RESEARCH PART F-TRAFFIC PSYCHOLOGY AND BEHAVIOUR
title: What's your type? A taxonomy of pedestrian route choice behaviour in cities
setting: street (Poznań city-centre street network; walking task from Theatre Bridge to the Old Brewery shopping mall and back, Euclidean distance 1,420 m)
design: mixed (walking task with smartphone GPS tracking + semi-structured in-depth interviews within 48 h; data-driven open coding, topic analysis and Weberian ideal-type typology; authors describe it as a qualitative study)
sample_n: 18 participants aged 20-42 (7 male, 11 female; mean age 23.5) (analytic unit: 36 GPS-tracked routes)
exposure: Perceived noise reported spontaneously in interviews as a 'dynamic element' of the walk: vehicular and tram traffic noise along major streets and noisy crowded areas (mapped in Fig. 4); no acoustic measurement; noise is one of several dynamic elements alongside crowds, weather, sun/shade and time of day
behaviour_measure: Pedestrian route choice on an origin-destination walking task (A to B and back): GPS-recorded routes with distance, duration and speed (Table 1, Figs 3 and 5-9), and interview-reported route decisions and avoidance of noisy/crowded streets used to derive five route-choice types (Table 2)
measurement_method: self-report (in-depth interviews prompted with the participant's GPS track); sensor-GPS-video (smartphone GPS route tracking)
key_finding: Noise emerged as one of the dynamic elements shaping pedestrian route choice: traffic and tram noise was reported to make walking along major streets tiring, the maintainer type (N=4) was characterised as highly sensitive to and avoiding noisy and crowded areas, and the spontaneous type (N=2) as sensitive to noise. The evidence is qualitative and rests on few noise-related quotes; no magnitude or GPS-based comparison of noise exposure is reported.
effect_stats: NR (qualitative; Table 2 dynamic elements: maintainer type N=4 'High sensitivity to weather conditions, time of day, noise, crowded and busy areas'; spontaneous type N=2 'Medium sensitivity to crowded and busy areas; sensitivity to noise'; section 4.1 pedestrian-vehicle interaction topic referenced by 6 participants, e.g. 'I get tired as I walk along major streets because of the traffic and noise' (IDI9, M))
